title: Unit 1 Quiz · Introduction to Data Science
instructions: 33 questions, 39 marks. You have 30 minutes; the quiz submits itself when time runs out.
Questions and options are shuffled, so your neighbour's screen will not match yours.
Multi-select questions need ALL correct options for the marks. Ordering questions give part marks for each item in the right place.
After submitting you will see your score and an explanation for every question.

questions.q: Which statement best describes data science?
options: A field that combines statistics, programming and domain knowledge to extract insight from data and support decisions
The process of storing large amounts of data in databases
Making charts and graphs in a spreadsheet
questions.explain: Data science is end-to-end: statistics + programming + domain knowledge → insight → decisions or data products. AI, storage and charts are only parts or tools.

questions.q: “November revenue was ₹5.5 lakh, the highest of the year.” Which level of the DIKW pyramid is this?
questions.explain: Raw orders were organised and summarised to answer what/when: that is Information. Knowledge would explain why (festive discounts); Wisdom would say what to do.

questions.q: In Drew Conway's Venn diagram, what is the overlap of programming skills and domain knowledge WITHOUT maths/statistics called?
questions.explain: Without statistics you can produce analysis that looks convincing but is wrong, so it is called the danger zone.

questions.q: Data created per year grows from 2 ZB to 32 ZB in 8 years. The compound annual growth rate is closest to:
Which ‘V’ of big data is about the quality and trustworthiness of data, for example “delhi ” and “Delhi” in the same column?
questions.explain: Veracity = how accurate and trustworthy the data is. Inconsistent spellings, duplicates and impossible values are veracity problems.

questions.q: Select ALL the genuine benefits of data science for a business.
options: Decisions based on evidence instead of guesswork
A guarantee that every decision will be correct
questions.explain: Data science improves the odds of a good decision, but it never guarantees every decision is correct: data can be biased and the world changes.

questions.q: Arrange the stages of the data science lifecycle in the correct order.
questions.explain: Problem → Collect → Clean → Explore → Model → Evaluate → Deploy/monitor, and then the cycle repeats with new questions.

questions.q: Which stage of a typical data science project usually takes the MOST time?
questions.explain: Practitioners consistently report that finding, cleaning and preparing data takes more time than building models.

questions.q: What does this code tell you about the dataset?
options: The number of exact duplicate rows
questions.explain: duplicated() marks every row that is an exact copy of an earlier row; .sum() counts them. In the lab it printed 8.

questions.q: Customer ages are recorded as 21, 22, 23, 24 and 250 (a typo for 25). What are the mean and the median?
questions.explain: Mean = 340 / 5 = 68. Median = middle value of the sorted list = 23. One bad value moved the mean by 45 years, which is why cleaning matters.

questions.q: A deployed model slowly becomes less accurate because customer behaviour has changed. What is this called?
questions.explain: Model drift: the world changes after deployment, so the model's patterns go out of date. That is why the last stage is deployment AND monitoring.

questions.q: Building and maintaining the pipeline that moves orders from the shop database into the data warehouse every night is mainly the job of a:
questions.explain: Data engineers build and maintain pipelines (ETL), databases and warehouses so that clean data is available to everyone else.

questions.q: Turning a trained churn model into a fast, scalable service that the mobile app calls thousands of times a second is mainly the job of:
questions.explain: ML engineers put models into production: packaging, scaling and serving them reliably.

questions.q: Talking to store managers and defining a success KPI such as “average rating ≥ 4.0 within 3 months” is mainly done by:
questions.explain: Business analysts gather requirements and translate business needs into measurable goals (KPIs).

questions.q: Which role's main question is “What will happen, and what should we do about it?”
questions.explain: Analysts mainly explain what happened; data scientists build models to predict and recommend actions.

questions.q: Which statement about AI, ML and DL is correct?
options: Deep learning ⊂ Machine learning ⊂ Artificial intelligence
Artificial intelligence ⊂ Machine learning ⊂ Deep learning
Machine learning and AI are completely unrelated fields
Data science is a subset of deep learning
questions.explain: AI is the broadest field; ML is the part of AI that learns from data; DL is the part of ML that uses deep neural networks.

questions.q: In machine learning, what goes in and what comes out?
options: Rules + data go in, answers come out
Data + answers go in, rules come out
Only answers go in, data comes out
Only rules go in, data comes out
questions.explain: Traditional programming: rules + data → answers. Machine learning: data + known answers → the computer learns the rules (the model).

questions.q: A 1990s chess program that only follows rules written by expert players is an example of:
questions.explain: It shows intelligent behaviour (AI) but nothing is learned from data, so it is not ML.

questions.q: In the lab, a model was learned from the data. Using it, what rating is predicted for an order delivered in 5 days?
A phone camera that recognises faces in photos most likely uses:
questions.explain: Image recognition is a classic deep learning task (many-layered neural networks trained on many images).

questions.q: Select ALL the examples that are real-life applications of data science.
options: Flagging a suspicious UPI payment in real time
Predicting food-delivery time from distance, traffic and restaurant load
Sending weather-based crop advisories to farmers
Typing a letter in a word processor
questions.explain: Fraud detection, ETA prediction and crop advisories all learn from data to support decisions. Typing a letter uses no data analysis.

questions.q: Every data science application shares the same skeleton. Which is it?
questions.explain: A costly problem, data that captures behaviour, a method that finds the pattern, and a decision that changes because of it.

questions.q: What does CRISP-DM stand for?
options: Cross-Industry Standard Process for Data Mining
Critical Research In Statistical Processing for Data Models
Cross-Integrated System Process for Data Management
Customer Retention Insight Standard Process for Data Mining
questions.explain: Cross-Industry Standard Process for Data Mining, created by an industry group in the late 1990s and published in 2000.

questions.q: Arrange the six phases of CRISP-DM in the correct order.
questions.explain: Business Understanding → Data Understanding → Data Preparation → Modeling → Evaluation → Deployment.

questions.q: In which CRISP-DM phase is the go / no-go decision made by checking the results against the business goal?
questions.explain: Evaluation checks whether the model meets the business success criteria set in Phase 1, and decides whether to deploy.

questions.q: While first exploring the dataset you discover 64 missing ratings, 8 duplicates and a misspelled city. Which CRISP-DM phase are you in?
questions.explain: Describing data and verifying its quality is Data Understanding. Fixing those problems comes next, in Data Preparation.

questions.q: True or false: CRISP-DM is strictly linear; once a phase is finished you never go back to it.
questions.explain: False. CRISP-DM is iterative: Data Understanding often changes the business question, modeling often needs more preparation, and Evaluation can restart the cycle.

questions.q: Which methodology is associated with SAS and has the steps Sample, Explore, Modify, Model, Assess?
questions.explain: SEMMA = Sample, Explore, Modify, Model, Assess (SAS). Unlike CRISP-DM it has no business-understanding step.

questions.q: A phone earns ₹2,000 profit if it sells and loses ₹1,500 if it does not. Past data says the chance of selling is 0.6. What is the expected value per phone?
questions.explain: 0.6 × 2000 − 0.4 × 1500 = 1200 − 600 = ₹600. Positive, so buying is a good decision on average.

questions.q: Page A: 4,000 visitors and 160 orders. Page B: 4,000 visitors and 200 orders. What is the lift of B over A?
Ice-cream sales and drowning cases both rise in summer. What is the best conclusion?
options: Correlation does not prove causation: hot weather drives both
Drowning causes people to buy ice-cream
questions.explain: A hidden third factor (summer heat) causes both. Two things moving together is correlation, not proof of cause.

questions.q: An A/B test gives z = 1.2. What should a data-driven team do?
options: Treat the difference as possibly due to chance and collect more data
Conclude version A is definitely better
questions.explain: |z| = 1.2 is below 1.96, so the difference is not statistically significant at 95%. Keep testing before deciding.

questions.q: What does “HiPPO” mean in data-driven decision-making?
options: Hypothesis in Probability and Population Outcomes
questions.explain: HiPPO = Highest Paid Person's Opinion: deciding by rank instead of evidence. Data-driven teams ask “what does the data say?”
